page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, utilizing 2 threads per core. The memory configuration consists of 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of memory per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations show a strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2693.38, placing it in the top 25% tier. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 21558.27 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9379.0. Memory bandwidth tests indicate average throughput, registering 1018.3 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 75.4 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, which assist in cryptographic and integer operations.

The primary tradeoff of the n2d-highcpu-16 is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:1, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications. However, this configuration provides a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. It is suited for tasks such as software compilation, where it achieved a Geekbench compiling score of 13457.0, as well as static web serving, text processing, and light LLM inference tasks.
